_comment: Frozen contract for the Emergency Response Sprint (RoboBoat Task 3).
Set from three successful runs -- two counter-clockwise, one clockwise.
Direction is not a property of the course: at the competition a light
beacon on the mark sets it at run time, so a configuration that only
works one way round is not a working configuration. Both directions are
in the samples for that reason.
'task_passed' delegates to the scorer's own rule -- entrance gate crossed
outbound, a full turn about the mark in the commanded direction with no
laundered counter-winding, gate crossed inbound, nothing touched. Counting
gates cannot express that.
The clearance floor is a fraction of the achievable maximum, as on the
channel, so it means the same thing if the gate width changes. Note how
much lower it is than the channel's: this gate is 2.4 m against 2.8 m, so
the ceiling is 0.466 m rather than 0.650 m AND the boat uses more of it.
0.20 is min - 4sd. The run-to-run spread here is 0.013, five times
tighter than the channel's -- threading one gate twice is a far more
repeatable thing to measure than threading ten different ones.
elapsed_s is drift, not a requirement. It is the competition score for
this task, so it must stay visible, but a wall-clock-sized regression is
not a safety failure and should not red the build on its own.
